lines.1: Om. Salutation to the glorious Mahapratisara.
lines.2: The Tathagatas of old attained suchness, the highest truth,
lines.3: by holding her dharani: to that Pratisara I bow.
lines.4: In battle, Shakra conquered many daityas, bearing her dharani on his banner:
lines.5: giver of victory in war, the formidable one, to that Pratisara I bow.
lines.6: By whose power Brahmadatta won a kingdom free of enemies:
lines.7: the goddess who grants rule over the whole earth, to that Pratisara I bow.
lines.8: Even one guilty of many crimes, devoted to her, won the right to rule:
lines.9: destroyer of the fear of weapons and the rest, to that Pratisara I bow.
lines.10: Merchants who remembered her gained jewels and came safely out of the ocean:
lines.11: soother of every affliction, to that Pratisara I bow.
lines.12: Here ends the hymn to the protecting goddess Mahapratisara.
lines.13: Om. Salutation to the glorious Mahamantranusarini.
lines.14: Empowered by the Buddhas, she gives the Buddhas' fearlessness and destroys fear
lines.15: for those sunk in the ocean of existence: salutation to Mantranusarini.
lines.16: By the mere utterance of her mantra, the six terrible calamities
lines.17: come to ruin: to the boon-giver, salutation to Mantranusarini.
lines.18: Those who follow her mantra, no other spells or seizing spirits
lines.19: can harm, nor those they love: salutation to Mantranusarini.
lines.20: After speaking her mantra, the Buddha uttered verses
lines.21: by which there is well-being everywhere: salutation to Mantranusarini.
lines.22: In this Kali age, bereft of a Buddha, she works for the good of the world:
lines.23: calmer of sin and evil portents, salutation to Mantranusarini.
lines.24: Here ends the hymn to Mahamantranusarini.
lines.25: Om. Salutation to the glorious Mahamayuri.
lines.26: A man could keep even a deadly black serpent close beside him
lines.27: by the power of her mantra: to that Mayuri I bow.
lines.28: Brahma and the other guardians of the worlds, by her dharani, attained
lines.29: each his own office: to that Mayuri I bow.
lines.30: The golden-gleaming peacock chanting her spell, the fool could not catch
lines.31: even with an unfailing snare: to that Mayuri I bow.
lines.32: By chanting her mantra, living things revived, even withered trees:
lines.33: the goddess who revives the dead, to that Mayuri I bow.
lines.34: Through contact with her mantra, the wind becomes a calmer of great calamities:
lines.35: giver of awakening to the Buddhas, forever, to that Mayuri I bow.
lines.36: Here ends the hymn to the protecting goddess Mahamayuri.
lines.38: Chanting her dharani, Rahula found well-being
lines.39: when harassed by all the seizing spirits: to Shitavati I bow.
lines.40: She cools the burning of sin, and the pox and other contagions:
lines.41: soother of the pains of cold and heat, to Shitavati I bow.
lines.42: For those who wear threads knotted with her mantra, for a hundred thousand leagues
lines.43: she guards the traveler: to Shitavati I bow.
lines.44: She who was proclaimed long ago by the sage dwelling in the charnel ground
lines.45: to calm the attacks of seizing spirits: to Shitavati I bow.
lines.46: For those overpowered by seizing spirits and by wind, who wear the knotted amulet,
lines.47: the calmer of the fear of seizing spirits: to Shitavati I bow.
lines.48: Here ends the hymn to the protecting goddess Mahashitavati.
lines.49: Om. Salutation to the glorious Mahasahasrapramardini.
lines.50: In the great thousandfold world, she who works for the good of thousands,
lines.51: mother of a thousand beings: I praise Sahasramardini.
lines.52: Through her, plague-struck Vaishali has had a great festival ever since:
lines.53: calmer of great epidemics, I praise Sahasramardini.
lines.54: Tamer of the evil-minded yakshas, rakshasas, and ghosts,
lines.55: destroyer of sin and calamity, I praise Sahasramardini.
lines.56: By reciting her dharani, the Lion of the Shakyas was protected
lines.57: from poison: bane of poison, I praise Sahasramardini.
lines.58: Medicine mixed with honey, the remover of every disease,
lines.59: the reviver of the dead in this world: I praise Sahasramardini.
lines.60: Here ends the hymn to the protecting goddess Mahasahasramardini.
